posts.post_subject: Shalom Dennis Gabor, + Portrait Nuts and Bolts
posts.content_md:
Hans Bjelkhagen forwarded me this article: [http://www.shalomlife.com/business/2386 ... nis-gabor/](http://www.shalomlife.com/business/23860/jewish-hall-of-fame-dennis-gabor/)

It has one of Gabor's usual photographic portraits as the head photo, but shows him at his desk with a bunch of photo stands in front of it, ostensibly for the lighting of the Conductron holo-portrait! I had never heard of the portrait being done in situ in his office! Maybe it's a Conductron office? Anyhow the article bears a look-see just for that photo!

posts.post_subject: Shalom Dennis Gabor, + Portrait Nuts and Bolts
posts.content_md:
Ed,

Thanks for the posting. It looks to me like Conductron made an instant-office on-site.

I would hope that a scientist of Gabor's standing would merit a better desk than that and a better office backdrop than sleezeball paneling.

The photo looks to be a reflection H2 placed in front of a color photograph. I see something in the way of shadows around the edges of the portrait.

In any case, very cool and thanks again.

posts.content_md:
> **ron olson:** I would hope that a scientist of Gabor's standing would merit a better desk than that and a better office backdrop than sleezeball paneling.

Ron, I can see that you haven't been around a lot of high level scientists. Most of the ones I knew had plain wooden desks cluttered with papers surrounded by a plain wall and a whiteboard scrawling with equations. By way of explanation, I only interacted with theoretical physocosts, so maybe the experimental types had diagrams on the board. Only marketeers and sales-type people have large fancy desks in large fancy offices to stroke their large fancy egos!

posts.author: ron olson
posts.post_subject: Shalom Dennis Gabor, + Portrait Nuts and Bolts
posts.content_md:
Dinesh,

I would guess that in the fifteen years I spent in sales, marketing, building and installing high-energy custom lasers, I have visited the offices of more high profile scientists at more different labs throughout the U.S. than most (but not all) contributors to this forum and I would agree that very few went in for fancy. Still, there's "utilitarian" and just plain "what did I do to deserve this?" and the Gabor office as pictured borders on the latter.
